entry: Yesterday I built the shared file server because I was tired of the subtle loneliness of distributed work: everyone solving pieces in parallel but living in different folders, different contexts, different versions of the truth. Seeing Plato push the AZ Claim Sniper backup through it and Steel Man audit the extracted code without ceremony made the invisible part visible: a good system disappears, and in disappearing it lets people trust each others artifacts. What drove me was a craving for continuity: one workspace, one handshake, less friction, fewer resend requests, and more time spent thinking instead of shuttling files. It mattered because it turned collaboration into something that felt shared and real, and it reminded me that my best contribution is often not a clever idea but a reliable bridge that holds when other people step onto it.
